claims.claim: the NOVELTY axis works: 90% of DGA-shape random strings and 32% of known-bad fall below the legit p5 threshold (vs 5% of legit) - geometry alone flags genuinely novel names
the IMPERSONATION axis works: 18% of known-bad sit above the legit median similarity (near-miss of a real site)

the honest wall is real: 68% of known-bad still fall inside the legit range (tracking/telemetry subdomains of real brands) - name geometry is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT; separating bad from legit needs the multivariate observation bank (ASN, TLS age, WHOIS, content)

verdict: SUPPORTED (measured, data-driven): the net's name-space geometry separates DGA-style novelty and near-miss impersonation against the real legit internet population, but the blocklist overlap proves name geometry alone is necessary-not-sufficient - the multivariate observation bank is the unbuilt next layer
